definitions.explanation: Used in academic, legal, and philosophical writing.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}と{政治|せいじ}は{不可分|ふかぶん}だ。
{言語|げんご}と{文化|ぶんか}は{不可分|ふかぶん}の{関係|かんけい}にある。
examples.english: Language and culture have an inseparable relationship.

examples.japanese: {環境|かんきょう}{問題|もんだい}と{経済|けいざい}{成長|せいちょう}は{不可分|ふかぶん}であり、{同時|どうじ}に{取|と}り{組|く}む{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: Environmental issues and economic growth are inseparable, and we need to address them simultaneously.

notes:
Composed of {不|ふ} (not) + {可|か} (possible) + {分|ぶん} (to divide). Describes things that cannot be separated or divided, whether conceptually or physically. Primarily used in formal, academic, and political discourse.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不可分|ふかぶん}の{関係|かんけい}: inseparable relationship
- {不可分|ふかぶん}に{結|むす}びついている: inextricably linked
- {一体|いったい}{不可分|ふかぶん}: united and indivisible

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {切|き}り{離|はな}せない: cannot be separated (more conversational)
- {密接|みっせつ}な: closely connected (emphasizes closeness rather than impossibility of separation)
- {表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}: two sides of the same coin (emphasizes complementary nature)
